newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay's 30-share index leaps 2.22 pct at close.
newsitem.headline: Bombay's 30-share index leaps 2.22 pct at close.

text.p: A flurry of buy orders from foreign funds and increased speculative bidding in blue-chip stocks boosted Bombay bourses at close on Thursday, dealers said.

"A lot of buying interest is coming in from foreign players," said Sanjeev Sangvhi, chief dealer at institutional brokerage James Capel B&K. "Basically, we are seeing positive news in the market. All this helps prices."
On Thursday, Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda reiterated his government's resolve to attract $10 billion in foreign investment every year and promised a series of moves to boost foreign investment.

"Foreign investment will be encouraged in core and infrastructure sectors, export and high-tech areas," Deve Gowda told an international business conference at the Confederation of Indian Industry's annual meeting in Calcutta.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Thursday that he expected growth of industrial production to pick up in the second half of 1996/97 (April-March).

"The second half by all accounts will be better than the first half and therefore I am confident that this year India's economy will do well," he said. "Robust growth in agriculture would strengthen the economy in 1996/97."
The government on Wednesday said the index of industrial production rose 9.8 percent in the first six months of 1996/97 against a 12.1 percent increase in the same period last year.

Bombay stocks have rallied over 3 percent since Monday on growing market optimism about government policy announcements. Funds were active buyers in Hind Lever, Bajaj Auto, L&T and MTNL and bought mid-cap stocks in the broader market, dealers said.
SBI was up 5.0 rupees to 255.0, Bajaj Auto 23.20 to 941.0, TISCO 2.50 to 188.75, ITC 7.0 to 330.0, Hind Lever 34.70 to 873.0, L&T 6.0 to 237.0, MTNL 7.0 to 238.0.
